{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q3","solution":"Principle: in free fall (negligible air resistance) the only force is gravity, so the acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s^2 downward at every point of the path.
At the highest point the ball momentarily stops changing from upward to downward motion, so its instantaneous velocity is v = 0.
The acceleration is still g, pointing down; it does not vanish at the top. If it did, the ball would stay at rest there.
So v = 0 and a points down: choice (B).","answer":{"choices":["B"],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"computation":"","uses":[],"alternatives":[]}]}

{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q5.a","solution":"Method: completing the square.
Take half the coefficient of x: -6/2 = -3, and square it: 9.
f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9 + 5
f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4
So h = 3 and k = -4.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":"(x - 3)^2 - 4","elements":[],"must_include":[]},"computation":"","uses":[],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q5.b","solution":"Use the completed-square form from part (a): f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4.
Since (x - 3)^2 >= 0, f(x) >= -4.
Equality holds when x = 3.
The minimum value of f(x) is -4, at x = 3.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":-4,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"computation":"(3-3)^2-4","uses":["Q5.a"],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q5.c","solution":"From part (a), f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4, so the vertex is (3, -4).

The x-intercepts are (1, 0) and (5, 0).

{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q2","solution":"Solve the linear equation by expanding and collecting like terms.
Expand the left side: 3(x - 2) = 3x - 6.
So 3x - 6 = 2x + 5.
Subtract 2x from both sides: x - 6 = 5.
Add 6 to both sides: x = 11.
Check: 3(11 - 2) = 27 and 2*11 + 5 = 27, so both sides agree.
The answer is (D) 11.","answer":{"choices":["D"],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"computation":"","uses":[],"alternatives":[]}]}

{"parts":[{"part_id":"Q4.a","solution":"Identify every force acting on the crate; each is drawn as an arrow starting on the dot.
Gravity: weight mg = 4.0*10 = 40 N, pointing straight down.
Floor: normal force N, pointing straight up; the floor is level and the rope is horizontal, so N = mg = 40 N.
Rope: tension T = 20 N, pointing horizontally to the right.
Floor: kinetic friction f = 0.25*40 = 10 N, pointing horizontally to the left, opposite the motion.
For consistent arrow lengths: N and mg are equal, T is half as long as mg, and f is half as long as T.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[{"label":"F_g (weight, mg)","kind":"force","direction":"down","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"F_N (normal force)","kind":"force","direction":"up","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"T (tension)","kind":"force","direction":"right","position":"starts on the dot"},{"label":"f_k (kinetic friction)","kind":"force","direction":"left","position":"starts on the dot"}],"must_include":[]},"computation":"","uses":[],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q4.b","solution":"Method: Newton's second law applied along the horizontal direction.
Vertical balance: N = mg = 4.0*10 = 40 N.
Kinetic friction: f = mu*N = 0.25*40 = 10 N.
Net horizontal force: F_net = T - f = 20 - 10 = 10 N.
Acceleration: a = F_net/m = 10/4.0 = 2.5 m/s^2.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":2.5,"unit":"m/s^2","rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":[]},"computation":"(20-0.25*4.0*10)/4.0","uses":["Q4.a"],"alternatives":[]},{"part_id":"Q4.c","solution":"Once the rope is cut, the tension force is gone.
Vertically, the weight and normal force still balance (40 N each), so there is no vertical acceleration.
The crate is still sliding, so kinetic friction f = 10 N still acts, opposite the motion (to the left).
This friction is now the only unbalanced force, so the net force is 10 N to the left.
Deceleration: a = 10/4.0 = 2.5 m/s^2, directed opposite the velocity.
The crate therefore keeps moving to the right but slows down at a constant rate until it stops.
Once at rest it stays at rest, because no horizontal force acts to start it moving again.","answer":{"choices":[],"value":null,"unit":null,"rel_tol":null,"accept_also":[],"expression":null,"elements":[],"must_include":["The crate continues moving to the right but slows down and eventually stops.","After the rope is cut there is no tension force on the crate.","Kinetic friction still acts on the crate, opposite its motion (to the left).","The weight and normal force still balance, so the net force is the friction force, opposite the velocity.","A net force opposite the velocity produces a deceleration, which is constant because friction is constant."]},"computation":"","uses":["Q4.b"],"alternatives":[]}]}
